paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log probabilities of clinically relevant tokens generated by the MistralV0.2-Base model before and after fine-tuning on six distinct medical specialty datasets—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—arranged along the horizontal axis. The vertical axis quantifies negative log probability on a linear scale ranging from approximately -27 (lowest probability) to -22 (highest probability), with tick marks at integer intervals. For each specialty group, a light blue bar represents the baseline MistralV0.2-Base model, while five additional bars—colored pale orange (Cardio), light orange (Gastro), medium orange (Infect), dark orange (Neuro), brown (Obstetrics), and dark brown (Pediatrics)—represent the same model fine-tuned on each respective specialty. Across all six groups, the baseline model consistently exhibits the highest (i.e., worst) negative log probability, indicating weaker token prediction performance prior to fine-tuning. Among the fine-tuned variants, the Gastro-tuned model generally achieves the lowest (i.e., best) negative log probability across most specialties, suggesting strong generalization or cross-specialty transferability. Notably, in the Infect group, all bars are relatively tall, with the baseline reaching approximately -23.5, indicating overall higher uncertainty for infectious disease terms. In contrast, the Cardio group shows the smallest vertical spread between baseline and fine-tuned models—approximately 1.5 units—suggesting limited performance gain from fine-tuning within its own domain. The bars within each group are not sorted by height, and no additional annotations or error bars are present.
